title: Establish SLO declaration format and deployment guardrails for model endpoints
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Goal: Define a single, machine- and human-readable SLO/SLI declaration format for model endpoints and a set of deployment guardrails that enforce error-budget-aware failover, circuit breakers, and load-shedding across regions and model variants. This ticket captures schema proposals, policy text for runtime enforcement, dashboards/alerts, and an ops rollout plan.

Scope: per-endpoint and per-model-variant SLOs (including chat, text-generation, embeddings, and reranking). Includes: schema definition, default SLI formulas, priority weighting rules for composite SLIs, error budget burn-rate thresholds for circuit breaker actions, and gateway load-shedding hooks. Not in scope: billing changes and per-customer contractual terms (handled by PM/legal).
acceptance_criteria: A JSON/YAML SLO declaration schema is approved and checked into repo (examples for chat, embedding, reranker)
Runtime implements parser for declarations and applies SLO config to endpoints in staging
Circuit-breaker policy enacted: automated partial degrade (model-variant fallback) and regional failover when burn-rate thresholds are crossed, with clear audit logs
Load-shedding hooks added to edge gateway with token-based admission control and documented heuristics
Dashboards and alerts: per-endpoint error budget burn-rate, composite SLO health, and a runbook for manual override
Postmortem test run: simulate a sustained 4x error-rate increase and validate automatic mitigation and alerting
schema_proposal_summary: We propose an SLO declaration with fields: name, target (percentage), measurement_window (rolling, days), primary_sli (metric + aggregation + success_criteria), secondary_slis (list), weights (for composite), backoff_policy (burn-rate thresholds -> actions), failover_priority (region/modelVariant ordering), retention_tag, diagnostic_tags. Declarations are stored as YAML under infra/slo-declarations/ and validated by CI.
recommended_slis:
- Success rate: request-level status code (200 + valid token parse) measured as ratio over 1h and 7d windows.
- Tail latency: p95 and p99 token-latency for generation endpoints (measured per-request and tokenized).
- Throughput preservation: tokens/sec achieved vs provisioned (for dedicated).
- Model correctness proxy: rerank agreement / embedding cosine stability for a small golden-set sampled per-hour.
burn_rate_policy:
- Green: burn-rate < 2 -> no automation.
- Observe: 2 <= burn-rate < 8 -> warn; increase sampling and surface in dashboard.
- Degrade: 8 <= burn-rate < 40 -> trigger model-variant fallback (lower-cost compatible variant) and reduce batch size to prioritize latency.
- Trip: burn-rate >= 40 -> close-incoming-sessions for non-priority routes via tiered circuit breaker and route 503 for best-effort customers; initiate cross-region failover according to failover_priority.
Actions are rate-limited and require an audit event. Burn-rate windows are computed over 10m and 1h rolling intervals.
circuit_breaker_actions:
1) Soft fallback: switch traffic percentage to a compatible lower-capacity variant (e.g., quantized model) with 20% initial shift, observe for 5m.
2) Aggressive fallback: shift 80% if error budget continues to burn.
3) Regional failover: route new requests to next region in failover_priority after confirming capacity via control-plane handshake.
4) Gateway-level shedding: drop best-effort requests by priority header and apply token-based admission (see 'gateway_policy').
gateway_policy: Admission control decisions use token-bucket per-customer plus global prioritized queues. Each request annotated with priority: critical, standard, best-effort. Best-effort is shed first. For chat endpoints with streaming, accept first N tokens then apply early-termination notice header. Implementation: edge-proxy plugin + runtime API hook to enforce backpressure decisions.
observability_and_alerting:
Dashboards: per-endpoint SLO health, burn-rate heatmap, p95/p99 latency by region and modelVariant. Alerts: high burn-rate (10m), SLO breach projection (1h), composite SLO degradation. Include runbook links and auto-created incident channel on page.
Links: doc links and PRs in 'links' field.
runbook:
Runbook highlights:
- Step 0: If automatic mitigation fired, check audit log and recent deploys.
- Step 1: Evaluate burn-rate and top contributing endpoints via dashboard.
- Step 2: If soft fallback active, monitor 5m for error rate drop; if not improved escalate to aggressive fallback.
- Step 3: For regional failover, confirm capacity handshake and coordinate with infra to avoid double-failover.
- Step 4: Post-incident, capture corrective action and update declaration if SLI mis-modeled.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra, and product. Agreed to aim for a declarative YAML with CI validation.
2026-03-04: Prototype schema v0.1 created and wireframes for dashboard panels drafted (PR opened).
2026-03-07: Runtime team built initial parser; staging hook applied for two internal endpoints. Observability queried per-request metrics and produced baseline burn-rate curves.
2026-03-10: Security reviewed edge-admission control concept; no high risks but recommended additional telemetry.
comments: Liam Chen (2026-03-05): Added example SLO declarations for chat and embedding endpoints to the PR. Need review from applied-ml on correctness metric definition.
Maya Rodríguez (PM) (2026-03-06): Note that customer tiers must be honored in gateway policy — added as label and example mapping in the spec.
Ravi Patel (SRE) (2026-03-09): Suggest we add a canary mode where the circuit-breaker actions are logged but not executed for 24h to validate thresholds before auto-enforcement.
